text: Enhedu said. She was already looking at the surrounding courses for anything else worth taking.

text: Zik ran his thumb across the scored spiral. The edges were old. Whoever had tried to erase it had done the work years ago, maybe decades. The wall had simply kept the evidence the way walls kept everything else—without comment, without loyalty, without any interest in whether the people who came later were ready to see it.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun was already copying the cluster onto a fresh scrap, her handwriting smaller and tighter than usual.
speaker: Narrator

text: The Collector said the locked drawers hold the ones who didn't stop. What if they also hold the names the city tried to cross out and couldn't quite finish?
speaker: Ninsun

text: They finished the survey because the contract required it and because leaving early would have told anyone watching that they had found something worth finding. Balag completed his measurements. Enhedu stacked the reusable stone. Zik wrote the load assessment in the dry, practical language the temple clerks preferred. Ninsun kept the new copy of the defaced seal and the half-erased name folded inside her map, separate from the rest.
speaker: Narrator

text: By late afternoon the work was done. The clerk paid them in full and did not ask why they had spent so long on one short section of wall. They walked back toward the lower districts in the order that had become habit, four people carrying an ordinary day's pay and one more piece of proof that the city's erasures were never as complete as it wanted them to be.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik flexed his left hand beneath the linen.
speaker: Narrator

text: Because whatever lay beneath the city no longer needed to call him every day.
speaker: Narrator

text: It already knew where he was going.
speaker: Narrator

text: About the wall someone had repaired three separate times simply to hide one damaged symbol and one ordinary name.
speaker: Narrator

text: The Collector had said his father eventually learned he had been asking the wrong question.
speaker: Narrator

text: Walking home through the evening crowds, Zik realized he had never asked what that question had been.
speaker: Narrator

text: For the first time since opening the tomb, that frightened him more than the answer.
